flashcard_questions.q: What resolution do print images need for professional quality?
What resolution do web images typically use?
What is a vector image made from?
flashcard_questions.a: Mathematical shapes defined by coordinates and equations.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can a vector image be scaled without losing quality?
flashcard_questions.a: The shapes are recalculated at each new size rather than stretched.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a bitmap image pixelate when it is enlarged?
flashcard_questions.a: Its existing pixels are stretched to fill a larger area.
Compression that permanently removes some data to reduce file size.
Compression that reduces file size without removing any data permanently.

flashcard_questions.q: Which image format uses lossy compression and suits photographs on the web?
Which image format supports transparency and uses lossless compression?
Which format suits simple graphics and short looping animations?
Which image format is the standard for professional printing at 300 DPI?
Which format is a scalable vector file supported by modern web browsers?

flashcard_questions.a: An unprocessed image captured directly from a camera sensor.

notes: 15 cards: 4 property-to-meaning (PPI, DPI, and their target resolutions), 3 term-to-definition, 2 causal, 5 format-to-use, 1 RAW card. One format per card as required; BMP dropped because the lesson says it is rarely used for distribution.
